sources.quayProps: VISUAL ESTIMATE: explicit render-only working clusters on the central quay and beside the sheds; all positions, yaw angles, counts, local offsets, dimensions, low-poly segment counts and weathered timber, metal, pale float, subdued orange and rope colours are artistic estimates, not surveyed harbour equipment. quayPropScale doubles equipment and spacing for readability across the broad quay; clusters occupy roughly 14 by 12 m each with stacked battened crates, hooped barrels, open-frame crab pots, fishing floats and spiral rope coils. Deterministic index variation is baked once into merged geometry. The street at x -1946..-1938, barn-door approaches, the Sail Loft plaza at z 781..819, boardwalk at x -1855..-1841 and pontoon gangway access remain clear. No gameplay, collisions, terrain, simulation, protocol or departure changes.
sources.floatingDocks: VISUAL ESTIMATE: four timber fingers use the existing pontoon rectangles; railed gangways hinge just inside the quay at about 2.54 m and descend east over an 8 m run to decks with 0.46 m mean freeboard. Segmented floats, rub rails, guide-pile collars and cleats move with each deck; piles stay fixed. Seven dedicated 3.8 m open dinghy hulls are instanced beside selected fingers with two slack mooring lines each. All dimensions, placements, tessellation and muted colours are artistic estimates. TUNING GUESS: sheltered wave response attenuates dock/boat heave to 0.28/0.55 of shared water sampling, bounded at 0.16/0.24 m; tilt is attenuated and bounded at 0.025/0.06 rad. Gangways stay attached as decks move; disabled or zero-amplitude waves give flat-water poses. Render-only: no collisions, mooring gameplay, terrain, simulation, protocol or departure changes.
sources.layout: VISUAL ESTIMATE / sandbox design: a horseshoe bay about 3.9 km east-west and 4.4 km north-south, open to the south through a 2.6 km mouth between two headlands. World x east, z south, metres from the known departure (0, 0). The mainland is a polygon of land (signed distance, perturbed by seeded fractal noise of coastNoise amplitude and wavelength so the shore gets coves and points); islands are rotated ellipses with the same perturbation. The departure, all buoys and the shoals lie well clear of land.
sources.relief: VISUAL ESTIMATE: low hills. A beach rises to beach.height over beach.width from the waterline, then hills approach hillHeight with an exponential rise length, modulated by reliefNoise (fraction of the hill height).
sources.seabed: VISUAL ESTIMATE / TUNING GUESS: depth falls away from each shore with a seeded nearshore slope between 1:60 and 1:20 and saturates at maxDepth, so the bay centre is about 20-25 m deep. Shoals are Gaussian bumps rising to topDepth below mean sea level, deep enough to float the hull but shallow enough to ground the daggerboard.
sources.grid: Render/chart bake only: heights sampled every cell metres over the bounds. Physics evaluates the analytic function directly.
sources.landmarks: Sandbox landmarks for bearings, not real aids to navigation. height is the structure above the ground at its foot; colours are VISUAL ESTIMATE.
sources.harbour: VISUAL ESTIMATE / sandbox design: Westcove Harbour on the west shore. Rectangles, applied in order so later ones win where blends overlap (world x east, z south, metres) are blended into the elevation: `reclaimed` land is flattened to `height` m above sea level (quay, breakwater mole, a terrace behind them), `dredged` water is deepened to at least `depth` m (the town above the quay steps up the hill in four terraces at about the natural ground height of each, so the banks between them stay short; `houses: true` terraces take town houses), `paved` rectangles get a crisp quay slab, and `edge` is the blend width in metres outside each rectangle. Boats spawn at `departure` heading `headingDeg`, in the basin the mole shelters. Pontoons, buildings, cottage rows (separate cottages with small gaps along each rectangle, fronts toward compass `facingDeg`) and the PIER light are VISUAL ESTIMATE dressing for the quay.
sources.roads: VISUAL ESTIMATE / sandbox design: The two roads of Westcove are contour lines of the baked terrain (Harbour Road at 8 m, Hill Road at 20 m above sea level, 260 to 1340 m south), smoothed and thinned to a point every 25 m or so, so they follow the hillside the way a real road would. A town with `layout: roads` has its houses placed in clusters along the roads of that town, facing downhill toward the water; the other towns scatter houses at random. Through the terraces behind the harbour, Harbour Road runs along the lowest terrace and Hill Road along the middle one, and a short Upper Lane serves the top terrace. Roads are drawn as flat gravel ribbons laid on the terrain.
sources.towns: VISUAL ESTIMATE: house counts and radii so the shore does not look bare. Houses are only placed on gentle, dry ground.
sources.grounding: TUNING GUESS: when the seabed is shallower than the daggerboard tip, penetration (m, capped at maxPenetration) pushes the boat toward deeper water (pushStiffness N/m along the seabed gradient) and damps its motion (damping N s/m^2 times penetration times velocity, yawDamping N m s/rad per metre of penetration). Sized so a Laser at full drive stops within a few metres of touching on a 1:40 slope, and slides back off when the sheet is eased or the boat is turned away. gradientStep is the finite-difference step, m.
